environmental.altitude: no performance degradation to 2000 m (6562 ft)
environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent noncondensing; 5 to 93 percent short term
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F) normal operation
environmental.storage-temp: -40 to 70 C (-40 to 158 F) in the shipping container

features.optics-qsfp28: 100 GbE QSFP28 and 40 GbE QSFP+, direct attach and active optical cables, breakout cables to SFP+
features.optics-sfp-plus: 10 GbE SFP+, 1 GbE SFP, SFP+ direct attach cable and active optical cable
features.timing: RJ-45 grandmaster clock port (GM), 10 MHz output, 1 PPS output
features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 switches in a ring with QFX5110 or QFX5100 members; also a Virtual Chassis Fabric leaf

management.oob: management port C0 (RJ-45, em0, with a second C0 SFP cage) and C1 (SFP, em1)
management.usb: one USB port for image updates

performance.latency: 550 ns (guide, Benefits of QFX5110, for the line)
performance.qsfp28-speeds: 100 GbE or 40 GbE; or four 10 GbE with a 40 GbE breakout cable
performance.sfp-plus-speeds: 10 GbE with SFP+ optics; 1 GbE with SFP optics; 100 Mbps from Junos OS 18.3R1
performance.switching-capacity: 960 Gbps aggregate throughput (guide, QFX5110-48S Hardware); see the throughput gap

physical.depth-note: 20.48 in (52.02 cm) excluding fan and power supply handles (Table 24)
physical.weight-note: 23 lb (10.43 kg) with two power supplies (Table 24)

power.power-input-ac: 90 to 264 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 3.6 A at 90 VAC (guide Table 14)
power.power-input-dc: rated -39 to -60 VDC, operating range -40 to -72 VDC, -8.2 A at 39 VDC (guide Table 19)
power.redundancy-note: two supplies, load-sharing and fully redundant; one may be removed and replaced while the switch runs

thermal.fans: five fan modules, hot-swappable; the switch runs 30 seconds without thermal shutdown while one is replaced

configs.description: QFX5110-48S-AFI: two 650 W AC supplies (JPSU-650W-AC-AFI) and five back-to-front fan modules (QFX5110-48S-FANAFI). All have a Juniper Azure Blue handle and the label AIR IN or AFI (guide Tables 11 and 13).
configs.name: ac-b2f

configs.description: QFX5110-48S-AFO: two 650 W AC supplies (JPSU-650W-AC-AFO) and five front-to-back fan modules (QFX5110-48S-FANAFO). All have a Juniper Gold handle and the label AIR OUT or AFO (guide Tables 11 and 13).
configs.name: ac-f2b

configs.description: QFX5110-48S-DC-AFI: two 650 W DC supplies (JPSU-650W-DC-AFI) and five back-to-front fan modules (QFX5110-48S-FANAFI). The front panel is the same.
configs.name: dc-b2f

configs.description: QFX5110-48S-DC-AFO: two 650 W DC supplies (JPSU-650W-DC-AFO) and five front-to-back fan modules (QFX5110-48S-FANAFO). The front panel is the same.
configs.name: dc-f2b

gaps.wanted: The guide gives the QFX5110-48S an aggregate throughput of 960 Gbps in its hardware overview, and 1.76 Tbps for the QFX5110 line in its list of benefits. No datasheet could be read to settle it. The 48S section is carried.
Table 19 gives the rated operating voltage as -39 to -60 VDC and the operating range as -40 through -72 VDC, with the current rated at 8.2 A at 39 VDC. Both are transcribed as printed.

The QFX5110 datasheet (the token is the nearest the schema offers: the document exists but was not readable). Its address redirects to an HPE document viewer (a00150813enw) that did not answer in three tries, so its ordering table, weight and power were not read.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port "for image updates" and gives no generation. It is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin.
The guide's text calls the 10 MHz and 1 PPS connections SubMiniature B (SMB); the photograph shows threaded jacks 7.5 mm across, drawn as the registry's SMA. The photograph is followed, estimated.
The studio photograph shows a green lamp in each upper corner of the GM jack. The guide's tables do not name them, so they are not modelled.

A photograph of the rear. The guide's drawing is the only picture: the fan numbers, the fan and power icons and the model chip are read from it, and the chip text is that of the drawing, not a confirmed print.
The laser-safety triangle at the lower right of the port side and the corner mark at the upper right. They are labels, not features of the metal, and are not drawn.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
`physical-context` on 7 bays (rear 7); `physical-context` on port groups qsfp28, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: guide Table 24: 1.72 in (4.3 cm) high, 17.36 in (44.1 cm) wide, 20.48 in (52.02 cm) deep excluding the fan and power supply handles, 23 lb (10.43 kg) with two power supplies. 1.72 in is 43.7 mm and 4.3 cm is 43 mm; the inch figure is carried, as the 1RU height. The width is the body: the mounting brackets are not part of it and are not modelled.

colour.note: The front plate samples #757a80 (a 15 by 20 px mean on the plate left of the SFP+ block, #7e8286 near the top edge) in the studio photograph. The photograph is lit and these are its values, not a paint reference. The rear has no photograph and carries the same chassis colour.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The guide's figure 14 marks the left coaxial jack with callout 6 (1 PPS output) and the right one with callout 5 (10 MHz output). The studio photograph prints PPS OUT under the left jack and 10M OUT under the right one, so figure and photograph agree and the render follows both. The guide's text calls the pair "SubMiniature B (SMB)" connectors; the photograph shows threaded SMA-style jacks 7.5 mm across, drawn as the registry's SMA (see gaps).

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide names the rack mount kit JNP-4PST-RMK-1U-E (a partial toolless four-post kit: a pair of front and rear mounting rails, a pair of mounting brackets and sixteen M4 x 6 mm screws, orderable as a spare), for rails 23.5 to 30.6 in (59.7 to 77.7 cm) apart front to back (Table 25), flush with the front of the rack or recessed 2 in (5 cm) with the extension bracket. Rack kits are recorded here and not modelled in this slice, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out. The modelled body is the 440.9 mm chassis, without brackets.

front-left.note: Left of the SFP+ block, read off the photograph at 3 times and scaled at 4.43 px/mm: the RJ-45 grandmaster jack (GM, callout 2) housing 125 to 199 px wide and 153 to 212 px high, so centred 17.6 mm from the left and 13.6 mm below the top; two gold coaxial jacks 7.5 mm across, PPS OUT centred at 17.2 mm and 10M OUT at 31.8 mm from the left, both 28.2 mm below the top; the ESD symbol at 7.0 mm, 31.8 mm and the ESD jack below it at 7.1 mm, 38.0 mm, 4.4 mm across. The lamps in the corners of the GM jack are green in the photograph; the guide names no function for them, so they are not modelled as lamps (see gaps).

gate-1.note: Front: the studio photograph. Its body is 1954 px wide (columns 84 to 2038) and 192.5 px high (rows 123.0 to 315.5), an aspect of 10.15 against the table's 440.9 / 43.7 = 10.09, 0.6 percent out. Scale 4.432 px/mm across and 4.405 down. Rear: figure 16, a raster drawing 1500 px wide whose body outline is 1449 x 146.5 px, an aspect of 9.89, 2 percent out; the positions along the width are taken at 3.286 px/mm and those down the height at 3.35 px/mm. Figure 14 is a 1500 px flat drawing of the front used only to count and to read the printing.

lifecycle.note: Searched the guide for an end-of-life notice and found none; the guide is dated 2026-09-24. No announcement for the QFX5110-48S was looked for at Juniper's end-of-life pages, so the device states none announced, estimated.

mgmt.note: Figure 17 and its key: em0 is the RJ-45 management port C0 (callout 2, lower jack), and the key's callout 2 also names an additional SFP management port, "the second C0" (upper SFP cage); em1 is the SFP management port C1 (callout 5, lower SFP cage); callout 3 is the RJ-45 console port CON (upper jack). The guide says that if both C0 ports are cabled the copper one takes priority. Table 9 gives the lamps. The drawing shows no lamps on the SFP cages.

modules.note: The fan modules (QFX5110-48S-FANAFO and QFX5110-48S-FANAFI, juniper/qfx5110-48s-fanafo and qfx5110-48s-fanafi) and the 650 W power supplies (JPSU-650W-AC-AFO, -AFI, -DC-AFO and -DC-AFI, reused from juniper/qfx5100-jpsu-650w-*) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. Guide Table 11 (pp. 40-41) names a fan module for each model and airflow, and p. 44 says to use only the one designed for the product number, so the 32Q has its own. The guide says to fit a blank panel over an empty power supply slot but names no part number for it, so no blank is modelled. Every 48S ships with two supplies and five fan modules (Table 3 has no chassis-only 48S).

port-lamps.note: Two dots flank each SFP+ numeral, the Link/Activity lamp on the left and the Status lamp on the right (guide Tables 5 and 7). They are read from the photograph at 4.4 px/mm: the left dot 2.6 mm and the right dot 3.2 mm either side of the cage centre, at 7.3 mm and 36.5 mm below the top edge. Four dots stand at 4.1 mm pitch above each upper QSFP28 cage and below each lower one, centred on the cage (Tables 5 and 6, bi-colour). The first lamp of a QSFP28 port is the link lamp of an unchannelized port; the other three are channel lamps (Table 6).

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off the photograph and figure 14: the SFP+ ports run 0 to 47, even above the upper row and odd below the lower row, the numeral between its two lamps; the QSFP28 ports are 48 and 49 down the first column, 50 and 51 down the second, the numeral above the lamps of the upper cages and beneath the cages of the lower ones, centred on each cage. The guide's own text numbers the SFP+ ports 0 through 47 and the QSFP28 ports 48 through 51. Interface names are not printed on the unit and the guide's front-panel text does not state them, so none is written to the manifest.

ports.note: Front photograph, dividers between cages found as bright columns across the opening: 24 columns of SFP+ cages on a pitch of 63.3 px, 14.28 mm, which is the registry's 14.25 SFP+ ganged pitch, in four groups of six. The groups start at 256, 649.5, 1043 and 1436.5 px, a stride of 393.5 px, 88.78 mm, so the gutter is 88.78 - 6 x 14.25 = 3.28 mm, and the first cage starts at 38.8 mm from the left edge. Then four QSFP28 cages in two columns, the first face from 1832 px, 394.4 mm, on a pitch of 84 px, 18.95 mm (the registry's 19.0 is used). Counts are 48 and 4, the guide's callouts 3 and 4 of figure 14. The cells use the registry's apertures (14.25 x 10.4 and 18.5 x 9.58); the photographed cage faces are 10.0 mm and 9.0 mm high because they include the bezel.

power.note: guide Table 14 (AC): 90 to 264 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 3.6 A at 90 VAC, typical 167 W and maximum 226 W for the 48S. Table 19 (DC): rated -39 to -60 VDC, operating range -40 through -72 VDC, -8.2 A at 39 VDC, the same 167 W typical and 226 W maximum. The guide's note: maximum measured at 40 C ambient with SR optics at 100 percent load with IMIX traffic; typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load with IMIX traffic, excluding transceivers. The AC pair is the device's, since AC is the default build; the DC feed is carried under its own keys.

rear-drawing-vs-text.note: Figure 16 draws back-to-front fans (AIR IN) beside supplies lettered AFO. The two cannot be mixed (Tables 11, 13 and 18), so the drawing mixes two builds. The default configuration here is front-to-back with Juniper Gold handles per Tables 13 and 18; the AFI configuration is the blue build. Figure 16 is not followed for the lettering.

rear-layout.note: Figure 16, the flat drawing of the FRU end, with figure 17 for the management panel, both read at 3.5 times. There is no photograph of the rear: the studio rear photograph returned a 404 page. At the left a 63.2 mm panel carries the QFX5110 and RUNNING JUNOS chip and the logo (not drawn), the four chassis lamps ALM, SYS, MST and ID, two stacked SFP cages (C0 above C1), the console and C0 jacks stacked in one shield, the USB port and the reset pinhole. Then five fan slots on a 48.95 mm pitch, each preceded by a fan icon, its number 0 to 4 and a status lamp, then two supply slots on a 60.8 mm pitch, each preceded by a power icon and its number 0 or 1. The fan and supply slots measure 40.9 x 41.6 mm and 54.8 x 39.8 mm, which are the sizes of the components that seat there. Every position is estimated from a drawing 2 percent out in aspect.

row-pitch.note: Down the SFP+ columns the cage faces run from row 169 to 212 and 230 to 270 px, centres 15.3 and 28.6 mm below the top edge, a row pitch of 13.4 mm (the QFX5100-48S reads 12.9; the two chassis are not the same). The QSFP28 faces run 171 to 210.5 and 230.5 to 270 px, centres 15.4 and 28.8 mm, a pitch of 13.4 mm. y is good to about 0.3 mm.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5110 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-09-24, 228 pages (Juniper Networks, address below; terms: the guide's copyright notice and the Juniper EULA it names, a reference copy kept outside the repository). Tables 3 (models and part numbers), 5 to 10 (lamps), 11 (fan modules), 13 and 14 (AC supplies), 18 to 20 (DC supplies), 22 (environment), 24 (physical specification); figures 12 and 14 (port panel), 16 to 19 (rear and management panel), 20 to 27 (fan modules, airflow and supplies). Juniper's studio photograph of the 48S front (image library, qfx5110-48s-front-high, 2100 x 508 px). The datasheet is at a Juniper address that redirects to an HPE document viewer (a00150813enw); it did not answer, so no datasheet figure is used and none is cited. The studio photograph of the rear (qfx5110-48s-rear-high) returned an HTML 404 page, so the rear has only the guide's drawings. No Visio stencil or 3D model was available, and none is named by the guide.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md): the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, so both lips face the band between the rows. In the photograph the latch tongues are at the foot of the upper cages and the top of the lower ones, which is the same thing; the QSFP28 pairs show the same.

vents.note: Two staggered rows of hexagonal holes along the top edge (1.6 to 5.7 mm), from 28.4 mm to the right end, so that the GM legend stands on solid metal, and one along the bottom (39.5 to 42.9 mm) from 10.4 mm. They are drawn as vent strips; the hexagon pitch is read off the photograph at 3 times and is estimated, as the pattern is a rectangular approximation of a staggered hexagon field.
